mainTopic: Whether one is liable for slaughtering outside an early אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו: proofs for רבי חלקיה against רב הונא
overview: This amud continues a discussion about an offering that is not yet ready to be brought (מחוסר זמן) and is slaughtered outside the Temple courtyard. The question is whether a person is liable for it. רבי חלקיה holds that one is liable for an early אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו, while רב הונא holds that one is exempt. The גמרא first sets aside the example of a year-round פסח, since that animal simply counts as a שלמים. It then tries two ברייתות as proof for רבי חלקיה. Each time it deflects the proof by saying the ברייתא may follow רבי אליעזר, who compares אשם to חטאת. A third ברייתא, reported by רב דימי from the school of רבי ליואי, is harder to push aside. רב דימי himself contrasts it with לוי's ברייתא and splits them into לשמו and שלא לשמו, and רב אשי does the same with the משנה. Finally, רב הונא escapes the refutation by limiting the ברייתא to a case of two אשמות set aside as a backup, where one of them is really an עולה from the start.

steps.title: The Paschal offering as a counter-example
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to a פסח brought during the rest of the year. It seems to be unfit for its own sake but fit when brought for a different sake.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at a פסח during the rest of the year: it is not fit if brought as a פסח, yet it is fit if brought for another purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case that seems to show an offering can be unfit for its own sake (לשמו) and still be fit for another sake (שלא לשמו).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion assumed that if an offering cannot be brought for its own purpose, it cannot be valid for any other purpose either. A פסח outside its proper time on ערב פסח seems to break that assumption. It cannot be brought as a פסח, yet when slaughtered for another purpose it is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The Paschal offering, normally brought on the afternoon of the 14th of ניסן
The rest of the days of the year
For its own sake, meaning slaughtered for the purpose it was set aside for
Not for its own sake, meaning slaughtered as a different type of offering

phrases.english: A Paschal offering during the rest of the days of the year,
which is not fit for its own sake,
but is fit not for its own sake!

steps.triggerLanguage: פֶּסַח בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה – דְּאֵינוֹ כָּשֵׁר לִשְׁמוֹ, וְכָשֵׁר שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion from the previous page by offering a counter-example to the assumption being tested there.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that an offering unfit for its own sake cannot be fit for another sake
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסח outside its time is unfit as a פסח but valid when slaughtered for another purpose, so the two can come apart.

steps.title: A year-round Paschal offering is really a peace offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a פסח during the rest of the year automatically counts as a שלמים, so it is not a real example.
steps.simpleTranslation: A פסח during the rest of the year is simply a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the counter-example. Outside its time, a פסח is treated as a שלמים, so it is not a case of an offering being 'fit for another sake.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only worked if the animal was still a פסח being slaughtered for a different purpose. The answer is that during the year it has already become a שלמים in its own right. So its validity comes from being a שלמים, not from being a פסח slaughtered שלא לשמו.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings
They are

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying the year-round פסח stops being holy. It is still a valid offering. It just counts as a שלמים rather than as a פסח brought for another purpose.

phrases.english: A Paschal offering during the rest of the days of the year
is a peace offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: פֶּסַח בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה – שְׁלָמִים נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counter-example of step 1 by re-defining what the year-round פסח is.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A year-round פסח is a פסח slaughtered שלא לשמו and still valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: A year-round פסח is itself a שלמים, so it proves nothing about offerings slaughtered שלא לשמו.

steps.title: A ברייתא that might support רבי חלקיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא supports רבי חלקיה. The ברייתא first raises the possibility of exempting offerings whose owners are not yet ready.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports him: I might have thought that I exclude even an עולה that is too early because of its owner, and an אשם נזיר and an אשם מצורע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a possible proof for רבי חלקיה from a ברייתא. Here the ברייתא only asks whether these premature offerings are excluded from liability for שחוטי חוץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These cases are different from an animal that is itself too young. Here the animal is fine, but the owner is not ready yet, such as a נזיר or מצורע who has not finished his process. The ברייתא raises the idea that slaughtering them outside the courtyard might carry no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it supports him
Lacking time, meaning not yet ready to be offered
Because of the owner, meaning the owner is not yet ready
The guilt offering of a נזיר
The guilt offering of a מצורע

phrases.english: Let us say that this supports him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי חלקיה from the earlier discussion.

phrases.english: One might think that I exclude
even a burnt offering that is premature because of its owner,
and the guilt offering of a nazirite and the guilt offering of a leper?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the פסח discussion to a suggested support from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חלקיה's view about an אשם מחוסר זמן slaughtered outside
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about which premature offerings bring liability for שחוטי חוץ

steps.title: The verse includes every case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the words שור, כשב, and עז that a person is liable in every case, even for these premature offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'ox' means in any case, 'lamb' means in any case, 'goat' means in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The verse lists three animals, and each one teaches liability no matter what, so even these premature offerings are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since each animal is named separately, the ברייתא reads each as including every situation. So slaughtering an עולה, אשם נזיר, or אשם מצורע outside does bring liability, even though the owner was not yet ready.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches
In any case, no matter what
Ox, lamb, goat

phrases.english: The verse states:
"Ox" means in any case,
"lamb" means in any case,
"goat" means in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא by answering its 'one might think' question.
steps.raayaObject: Liability for premature offerings slaughtered outside
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 17:3, the words שור, כשב, עז

steps.title: The ברייתא leaves out the sin offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the ברייתא lists אשם but not חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yet the חטאת it left out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what is missing. The ברייתא names the אשם of a נזיר and of a מצורע, but it does not mention their חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This missing case is the key to the proof. If the ברייתא had a reason to include אשם and leave out חטאת, that reason may be exactly what supports רבי חלקיה.

keyTerms.meaning: Whereas, yet
Sin offering
It left it out

phrases.english: whereas a sin offering, it left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an observation from the ברייתא quoted in steps 3-4.
steps.raayaObject: Why אשם is included and חטאת is not

steps.title: Which case is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means. It rules out an offering slaughtered at its proper time, because then a חטאת would bring liability too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with? If you say at its proper time, why mention specifically an אשם? Even a חטאת would also bring liability!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which situation the ברייתא is describing. It rejects the first option, that the offering was slaughtered at its proper time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the offering was slaughtered outside at its proper time, a חטאת would bring liability just like an אשם. That would leave no reason to name only the אשם. So the 'proper time' reading cannot explain why חטאת was left out.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
If you say
At its proper time
Why specifically this case?

phrases.english: What are we dealing with?
If we say it is at its proper time,
why specifically a guilt offering?
Even a sin offering too!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the missing חטאת from step 5 to work out what case the ברייתא is describing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא is speaking of an offering slaughtered at its proper time or before it

steps.title: It must be before its proper time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is talking about an offering slaughtered before its proper time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is talking about one slaughtered not at its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles on the other option: the ברייתא means an אשם slaughtered before the נזיר or מצורע was ready. This narrows the case as the proof continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the 'proper time' reading is ruled out, the ברייתא must mean the premature case. That fits its opening words about offerings that are מחוסר זמן because of the owner. It also brings the ברייתא closer to רבי חלקיה's case of an אשם מחוסר זמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather
Not at its proper time

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא reads the ברייתא as talking about the premature case, because it leaves out חטאת. Step 10 will overturn this and read it as an אשם at its proper time.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not at its proper time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 after the first option was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is speaking of an offering slaughtered before its proper time.

steps.title: With what intention was the offering slaughtered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what intention the ברייתא is talking about. It suggests that the case cannot be לשמו, because then an early אשם would be unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what case is this? If you say it was slaughtered for its own sake, why is he liable for the אשם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks whether the slaughterer had the right intention (לשמו) or the wrong one (שלא לשמו). It tests the first option, and this sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said the case is an offering slaughtered before its time. Such an אשם is unfit, so slaughtering it outside should bring no liability. Since the ברייתא says he is liable, the case of לשמו seems not to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: With what? In what case?
If you say
For its own sake (with the correct intention for this offering)
Why?

phrases.english: And with what [case are we dealing]?
If you say [it was slaughtered] for its own sake –
why is he liable for an אשם?
phrases.notes: An early אשם is unfit inside the Temple too, so why should he be liable for slaughtering it outside?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the intention behind the slaughter in the case Step 7 defined
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא is talking about slaughter לשמו or שלא לשמו
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It cannot be לשמו, since an early אשם would then be unfit and bring no liability

steps.title: So the case must be not for its own sake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the case must be שלא לשמו. If so, the ברייתא supports רבי חלקיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it talking about slaughter not for its own sake?
steps.whatsHappening: Having ruled out לשמו, the גמרא suggests the case must be שלא לשמו. If so, the ברייתא would support רבי חלקיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by process of elimination. If the ברייתא makes a person liable for slaughter שלא לשמו, that fits רבי חלקיה's position.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? (introduces a conclusion that seems forced)
Not for its own sake (with the wrong intention)

phrases.english: Rather, is it not [talking about slaughter] not for its own sake?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the remaining option after Step 8 ruled out לשמו
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that makes a person liable for slaughtering an אשם outside, read as slaughter שלא לשמו

steps.title: Actually, it is on time and not for its own sake, following רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא is talking about an אשם slaughtered at its proper time but שלא לשמו. It follows רבי אליעזר, who compares אשם to חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is talking about slaughter at its proper time and not for its own sake. The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, who says we compare an אשם to a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and gives a different case: an אשם slaughtered on time but with the wrong intention. It explains that this ruling follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו is still fit, so there would be no reason to think he is exempt outside. But רבי אליעזר compares אשם to חטאת, which becomes unfit שלא לשמו. So we might have thought he is exempt, and the ברייתא needs the פסוק to teach that he is liable. This takes away the support for רבי חלקיה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (introduces a new reading of the case)
At its proper time
We compare (two things learned together from one פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: Step 7 said the case was before its proper time. This step drops that and puts the case at its proper time, with the problem being the wrong intention instead.

phrases.english: Actually, [it is] at its proper time and not for its own sake;
and it is [the view of] רבי אליעזר,
who says: we compare an אשם to a חטאת.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:7: "as is the חטאת, so is the אשם."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 9 by giving a different case
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of the ברייתא as support for רבי חלקיה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as an on-time אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו, following רבי אליעזר, so it does not need to follow רבי חלקיה

steps.title: The ברייתא named the secondary case, but the main case is the same
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the אשם, which is learned from the חטאת. The same rule applies to the חטאת itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא taught the secondary case, and the same is true of the main case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא mentioned only אשם and not חטאת, the question raised in Step 5. The חטאת was left out, but it has the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי אליעזר's view, the rule for אשם is borrowed from חטאת, so אשם is the secondary case. The ברייתא chose to mention the secondary one. This does not mean the חטאת is different; slaughtering it outside שלא לשמו also makes a person liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Secondary, the case learned from another
The main case, the source of the rule
And the same law applies

steps.whatToRemember: Final reading of the ברייתא: an אשם slaughtered outside at its proper time but שלא לשמו, following רבי אליעזר. The same is true of a חטאת, so the ברייתא is no proof for רבי חלקיה.

phrases.english: And [the תנא] taught the secondary case,
phrases.notes: The secondary case is the אשם, since it learns its rule from the חטאת; the main case is the חטאת.

phrases.english: and the same is true of the main case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the new reading from Step 10 by explaining why only אשם is listed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the ברייתא chose its wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since only אשם is listed, a חטאת in this case must not bring liability
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא listed the secondary case, and the חטאת has the same rule

steps.title: A new ברייתא about early עולה and חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא to support רבי חלקיה. It opens by suggesting that liability might include an early עולה and an early חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one might think that I include an עולה that is too early because of the animal itself, and a חטאת that is too early either because of the animal or because of the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new attempt at proof with a different ברייתא. This line only opens the ברייתא; the proof comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה can be too early only because of the animal itself, for example if it is less than eight days old. A חטאת can be too early because of the animal or because its owner is not yet ready to bring it. The ברייתא raises including all of these in liability, and the next lines will show what it decides.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering whose time has not yet come
Because of the animal itself
Because of the owner
Burnt offering

phrases.english: Come and hear:
one might think that I include [in liability]
an עולה whose time has not come – because of the animal itself,
and a חטאת – whether [early] because of the animal itself or because of the owner?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה עוֹלַת מְחוּסַּר זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, starts a new proof from a different ברייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about slaughtering early offerings outside (עולה early in itself; חטאת early in itself or because of its owner)

steps.title: The verse limits liability, and the אשם is left out
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers its own opening suggestion with a פסוק. An offering that cannot be brought to the entrance of the אהל מועד carries no liability. The ברייתא does not list the אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting." Anything that is not fit to come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, one is not liable for it. But the guilt offering was left out of the list.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its point: an early offering that is unfit for the entrance of the אהל מועד carries no liability. The גמרא notices that the אשם is missing from the list of exempt cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first considered making one liable for an early עולה and חטאת. The פסוק teaches that unfit offerings carry no liability. Since an early אשם is not listed, it seems one IS liable for it, and the גמרא wants to use that silence as a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse teaches": introduces the פסוק that settles the question
The entrance of the Tent of Meeting, meaning the proper place for offering
Fit (to be offered)
He left it out (of the list)

phrases.english: The verse states: "And to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting"

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לָבֹא בְּפֶתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד,
phrases.english: anything that is not fit to come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,
one is not liable for them.
But the guilt offering, he left it out;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא opened in step 12 and draws an inference from what it leaves out.
steps.raayaObject: That one is liable for slaughtering an early אשם outside the עזרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's omission of the אשם from the exempt list

steps.title: What kind of slaughter is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means. It cannot be לשמו, because then an early אשם should be exempt too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with? If you say it was slaughtered for its own sake, then the guilt offering should also be exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which case the ברייתא has in mind, so it can understand why the אשם was left out. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal was slaughtered לשמו, an early אשם is just as unfit as an early חטאת. So the ברייתא should have exempted the אשם as well. Leaving it out makes no sense in a לשמו case.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
Slaughtered for the sake of its own type of offering
Let him be exempt

phrases.english: What are we dealing with?
If you say it was for its own sake,
then let the guilt offering also be exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which case lies behind the inference from step 13, in the same way as step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ברייתא is discussing slaughter לשמו or שלא לשמו

steps.title: The case must be שלא לשמו, which supports רבי חלקיה
steps.stepSummary: The case must be שלא לשמו. Then a חטאת is unfit but an אשם is still fit, so one is liable for the אשם, just as רבי חלקיה says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it talking about slaughter not for its own sake?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא must be talking about שלא לשמו. That reading supports רבי חלקיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת slaughtered שלא לשמו is disqualified, so one is exempt for slaughtering it outside. An אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו is still kosher, so it is fit, and one is liable. That explains why the ברייתא left the אשם out.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it...? (introduces the only reading left)
Slaughtered for the sake of a different offering

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about one slaughtered not for its own sake?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion that step 14 forced, matching step 9.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second ברייתא, read as a שלא לשמו case

steps.title: The ברייתא may follow רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The case really is שלא לשמו. But the ברייתא may follow רבי אליעזר, who compares אשם to חטאת, so an אשם שלא לשמו is unfit too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is about slaughter not for its own sake, and it follows רבי אליעזר, who compares the guilt offering to the sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. It agrees the case is שלא לשמו, but says the ברייתא may follow רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אליעזר, an אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו is disqualified just like a חטאת. So an early אשם is also exempt, and the ברייתא no longer shows liability for it. This removes the support for רבי חלקיה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually (keeps the earlier reading but adds a twist)
Compares one law to another, so they share rules

phrases.english: Actually, it is about one slaughtered not for its own sake,
and it follows Rabbi Eliezer,
who compares the guilt offering to the sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ, וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 15, in the same way as step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. רבי חלקיה's view itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that an אשם שלא לשמו is kosher, but רבי אליעזר holds it is unfit like a חטאת.

steps.title: The ברייתא lists only the main case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא left out the אשם because it mentioned the main case, the חטאת. The same rule applies even more so to the אשם, which is learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught the main case, and all the more so the secondary case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא skipped the אשם if it is also exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאת is the source of this rule, and the אשם only learns from it. A ברייתא that teaches the source does not need to spell out the case that follows from it. So leaving out the אשם proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The main or source case (here, the חטאת)
The secondary case that is learned from the main one (here, the אשם)
All the more so

steps.whatToRemember: The second ברייתא, like the first, does not prove רבי חלקיה's view. It may follow רבי אליעזר and mention only the חטאת as the main case.

phrases.english: He taught the primary case,
and all the more so it applies to the secondary case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rejection by explaining the ברייתא's wording, in the same way as step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording: the ברייתא lists the main case and leaves out what is learned from it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving out the אשם shows that one is liable for it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אשם was left out only because it follows from the חטאת.

steps.title: רב דימי's ברייתא: liability for offerings early because of the owner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new proof for רבי חלקיה. A ברייתא from the school of רבי ליואי teaches that one is liable for an עולה, an אשם נזיר or an אשם מצורע that is early because of its owner. רב דימי says a פסוק was given for this, but he does not know which one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: when רב דימי came, he said that the school of רבי ליואי taught: You might think I exclude even a burnt offering that is early because of its owner, a nazirite's guilt offering and a leper's guilt offering. From where do we know otherwise? They brought a verse to teach liability, but I do not know what it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ברייתא to support רבי חלקיה. It says one is liable for slaughtering outside offerings that are early only because their owner is not yet ready.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the offering is early only because of the owner, and the ברייתא still makes one liable. That fits רבי חלקיה. רב דימי remembers the ruling but not the פסוק it came from.

keyTerms.meaning: Early because of its owner, whose time has not yet come
The guilt offering of a נזיר
The guilt offering of a מצורע
To make one liable

phrases.english: Come and hear:
for when Rav Dimi came, he said,
the school of Rabbi Livai taught:
You might think that I exclude
even a burnt offering that is early because of its owner,
a nazirite's guilt offering and a leper's guilt offering;
From where do we know otherwise?
And they brought a verse for them, to make one liable,
but I do not know what it is.
phrases.notes: רב דימי is speaking here: he knows the ruling but forgot which פסוק was used.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second proof was rejected, the גמרא brings a new source to support רבי חלקיה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חלקיה's view that one is liable for certain early offerings slaughtered outside
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the school of רבי ליואי, as reported by רב דימי

steps.title: Which verse teaches this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the פסוק behind the ברייתא of the school of רבי ליואי.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the source in the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי said a פסוק was given for this rule but did not know which one. Now the גמרא asks which פסוק it is, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says one is liable for slaughtering outside an offering that is early because of its owner. Liability for slaughtering outside needs a source in the Torah, so the גמרא looks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the source? Literally, what is the learning?

phrases.english: What is the source?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the פסוק that רב דימי could not identify.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק makes one liable for slaughtering outside an offering that is early because of its owner.

steps.title: Ox, lamb, goat: in any case
steps.stepSummary: רבינא learns it from the words 'ox, lamb, goat' in the פסוק about slaughtering outside. Each word means 'in any case,' even when the animal is early.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: 'Ox' means in any case, 'lamb' means in any case, 'goat' means in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives the source. The פסוק about slaughtering outside names each animal, and this teaches that it applies in every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have just said 'an animal.' Naming each kind adds the idea that it counts in any case, even when it is early because of its owner. This supports רבי חלקיה, who says one is liable for an early אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, without limits
Ox, lamb, goat, the animals named in the פסוק

phrases.english: Ravina said:
"Ox": in any case,
"Lamb": in any case,
"Goat": in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra naming of each animal ('ox, lamb, goat') teaches liability in any case, even when the offering is early.

steps.title: Why is this a contradiction at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why this ברייתא should be a contradiction to רב הונא. It can be explained the way the גמרא said before.
steps.simpleTranslation: What contradiction is this? Answer it as you said before!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on using this ברייתא as a proof against רב הונא. It says the earlier answer can simply be used again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 10), the גמרא rejected a proof from the same 'ox, lamb, goat' ברייתא. It said the ברייתא speaks of an אשם at its proper time slaughtered שלא לשמו, following רבי אליעזר. The same move could work here, so the ברייתא would not prove רבי חלקיה right.

keyTerms.meaning: A contradiction, a clash between two sources
As you said before

phrases.english: What contradiction is this?
As you said!
phrases.notes: He's pointing back to the earlier answer about this same 'ox, lamb, goat' ברייתא: an אשם at its proper time slaughtered שלא לשמו, following רבי אליעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the proof from steps 18 and 20 really works.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof for רבי חלקיה against רב הונא from the ברייתא of the school of רבי ליואי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be explained the way the earlier one was, so it does not force רבי חלקיה's view.

steps.title: רב נחמן: רב דימי set two ברייתות against each other
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains why the old answer does not work for רב דימי. רב דימי set the ברייתא of the school of רבי ליואי against a ברייתא of לוי. לוי's ברייתא begins by saying that an אשם נזיר or אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמו is fit, but does not count for the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Because רב דימי set the ברייתא of the school of רבי ליואי against what לוי taught: An אשם נזיר and an אשם מצורע slaughtered not for their own sake are fit, but they do not count for the owner's obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן begins to explain why רב דימי could not use the old answer. This step sets up the contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי saw a clash between two ברייתות. That shows he read the ברייתא of the school of רבי ליואי as being about an offering that is truly early, not one at its proper time. The first part of לוי's ברייתא gives the normal rule: slaughtered שלא לשמו, these offerings are still fit.

keyTerms.meaning: He sets one source against another
The guilt offering of a נזיר and of a מצורע
They do not count for the owner's obligation

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
Because he set against each other
what the school of Rabbi Livai taught
and what Levi taught:
The guilt offering of a nazirite and the guilt offering of a leper
that one slaughtered not for their own sake are fit,
but they do not count for the owner's obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מִשּׁוּם דְּרָמֵי דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי לֵיוַאי אַדְּתָנֵי לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pushback of step 21 by showing how רב דימי himself read the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows from רב דימי's own contradiction how he understood the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא of the school of רבי ליואי could be about an offering at its proper time, following רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב דימי treated it as being about a truly early offering, since he contrasted it with לוי's ברייתא.

steps.title: לוי: an early אשם is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: לוי's ברייתא goes on: if they were slaughtered while early because of the owner, or when the lambs were in their second year, they are disqualified. That clashes with the school of רבי ליואי, which says one is liable for such an early offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered them when they were early because of the owner, or when they were in their second year, they are disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the clash itself. לוי says an early אשם is disqualified, while the school of רבי ליואי said one is liable for it outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an offering is disqualified, one is not liable for slaughtering it outside. So לוי's ruling seems to go against the ברייתא of the school of רבי ליואי, which says one is liable for the same early offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Early because of the owner: the owner is not yet ready to bring it
In their second year, too old for an offering that must be under a year
Disqualified

steps.confusionAlert: 'Early because of the owner' does not mean the animal is too young. The animal is fine; the owner is the one who is not yet ready to bring it.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered them when they were early because of the owner,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ בְנֵי שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים וּשְׁחָטָן –
phrases.english: or if they were in their second year and he slaughtered them,
they are disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting לוי's ברייתא and brings out its clash with the school of רבי ליואי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of the school of רבי ליואי, which makes one liable for an offering that is early because of its owner.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לוי calls that same early offering disqualified, and one is not liable for slaughtering a disqualified offering outside.

steps.title: רב דימי: לשמו versus שלא לשמו
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that there is no contradiction. לוי's ברייתא is about an offering slaughtered לשמו, so it is disqualified. The ברייתא of the school of רבי ליואי is about one slaughtered שלא לשמו, so one is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב דימי answers: It is not difficult. Here it is for its own sake; there it is not for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי settles the clash by splitting the cases. One ברייתא speaks of slaughtering לשמו and the other of slaughtering שלא לשמו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An early offering slaughtered לשמו is disqualified, so there is no liability outside. Slaughtered שלא לשמו, it is treated like a fit offering, so one is liable outside. This is exactly רבי חלקיה's view, which is why רב נחמן said רב דימי could not use the old answer.

keyTerms.meaning: He answers, he resolves the problem
It is not difficult, there is no contradiction
Here... there: splitting two sources into two cases

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב דימי, an אשם that is early because of its owner is disqualified if slaughtered לשמו. If slaughtered שלא לשמו, one is liable for slaughtering it outside. This matches רבי חלקיה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב דימי himself read the ברייתא as being about a truly early offering slaughtered שלא לשמו. That makes it real support for רבי חלקיה.

phrases.english: And Rav Dimi answers:
It is not difficult;
here, it is for its own sake,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is לוי's ברייתא, which says disqualified.

phrases.english: there, it is not for its own sake.
phrases.notes: 'There' is the school of רבי ליואי, which says liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁנֵּי רַב דִּימִי: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן לִשְׁמוֹ, כָּאן שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות disagree about an early אשם.
steps.terutzMaskana: לוי speaks of slaughtering לשמו (disqualified); the school of רבי ליואי speaks of slaughtering שלא לשמו (liable outside).

steps.title: רב אשי sets the משנה against the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי raises a contradiction between the משנה, which exempts one who slaughters an early offering outside, and the ברייתא, which makes him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי pointed out a contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא, רב אשי, raises his own version of the contradiction. This step sets up the answer that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי set two ברייתות against each other. רב אשי instead sets the משנה, which says one is exempt for an early offering slaughtered outside, against the ברייתא of the school of רבי ליואי, which says one is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises a contradiction (literally, 'throws' one source against another)
Our משנה
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: Rav Ashi raises a contradiction
between the mishna and the baraita,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel to רב דימי's contradiction, but this time the משנה is set against the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the משנה and the ברייתא of the school of רבי ליואי fit together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה exempts one who slaughters an early offering outside, but the ברייתא makes him liable.

steps.title: For its sake versus not for its sake
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the משנה is about an offering slaughtered לשמו, and the ברייתא is about one slaughtered שלא לשמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answers: Here it is for its sake, and there it is not for its sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי settles the contradiction by saying the two sources are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the early אשם is slaughtered לשמו, as an אשם, it is not fit, so slaughtering it outside does not make one liable. That is the משנה. If it is slaughtered שלא לשמו, it counts as a fit offering, so slaughtering it outside does make one liable. That is the ברייתא. This is the same split רב דימי used in Step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: And he answers (resolves the problem)
For its sake, meaning slaughtered as the offering it really is
Not for its sake, meaning slaughtered as a different kind of offering

phrases.english: And he answers: Here, for its sake,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the משנה, where one is exempt.

phrases.english: and there, not for its sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁנֵּי: כָּאן לִשְׁמוֹ, וְכָאן שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's own contradiction from Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different way of slaughtering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא give opposite rulings about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about לשמו (exempt), and the ברייתא is about שלא לשמו (liable).

steps.title: Is this a refutation of רב הונא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב אשי's answer refutes רב הונא, who holds that one is exempt even for an early אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב הונא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רב אשי's answer into a challenge against רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי read the ברייתא as saying one is liable for an early offering slaughtered שלא לשמו. רב הונא holds the opposite: in that case one is exempt. So it now looks as though the ברייתא goes against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא is testing)
A refutation, a strong challenge that would knock down a view

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav Huna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב אשי's reading of the ברייתא from Step 26 to challenge רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that one is exempt for an early אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו outside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רב אשי, the ברייתא makes one liable in exactly the case where רב הונא says one is exempt.

steps.title: רב הונא: the case of two guilt offerings set aside as a backup
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the ברייתא is about someone who set aside two אשמות as a backup. One of them is really an עולה from the start, so he is liable for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא could say to you: What are we dealing with here? A case where he set aside two guilt offerings as a backup, since one of them is a burnt offering from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends himself by saying the ברייתא is about an unusual case, not about every early אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person set aside two animals for one אשם, so that he would still have one if the first got lost. Only one of them will be brought as his אשם, so the other one is treated as an עולה from the start. That is why he is liable when he slaughters it outside. A normal early אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו still exempts him, just as רב הונא said.

keyTerms.meaning: What are we dealing with here? (the גמרא is about to limit a source to a specific case)
As a backup or guarantee, in case the first animal is lost
Guilt offerings (plural of אָשָׁם)
Burnt offering

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי reads the ברייתא as being about שלא לשמו. רב הונא survives the challenge by limiting the ברייתא to a special case: two אשמות set aside as a backup, where one of them is really an עולה from the start.
steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא does not say every early אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו makes one liable. He limits the ברייתא to the case of a backup animal, so his own rule of 'exempt' still stands.

phrases.english: Rav Huna could have said to you:
What are we dealing with here?
phrases.notes: "Here" means the ברייתא that makes one liable.

phrases.english: for instance, where he separated two guilt offerings as a guarantee,
since one of them is a burnt offering from the outset;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב הונא from Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא: limiting the ברייתא to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא makes one liable for any early אשם slaughtered שלא לשמו, which goes against רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is only about a backup animal that is treated as an עולה from the start, so רב הונא's rule still stands.
